items.value: CPF relief for employees = compulsory employee contributions on Ordinary Wages (up to the OW ceiling) and Additional Wages (up to the AW ceiling), counted within the S$80,000 overall relief cap. Voluntary contributions in excess of the compulsory amount under the CPF Act do NOT qualify - EXCEPT voluntary contributions to the MediSave Account, which IRAS says do qualify for relief. Also excluded: contributions on AW above the cap where the employee has two or more related employers, and contributions made during an overseas secondment/posting. Maximum compulsory relief for age 55 and below = 20% x S$102,000 = S$20,400 (derived).
items.evidence_quote: Employees can claim relief on compulsory employee CPF contributions and on voluntary contributions to their MediSave Account
items.note: Correction is to the blanket 'voluntary contributions are not deductible': IRAS excludes voluntary contributions above the compulsory amount but allows relief on voluntary MediSave contributions (subject to its own limits, which I did not retrieve - see IRAS page 'Compulsory and voluntary MediSave contributions'). The rest of the candidate is confirmed: IRAS worked examples cap OW at the yearly ceiling (using $7,400/month for 2025) and AW at the remainder of $102,000; the $80,000 cap covers 'the total of all tax reliefs claimed, including relief on compulsory and voluntary CPF contributions'. The S$20,400 maximum is arithmetic (20% x $102,000), not a figure I saw quoted by IRAS; month-by-month dropping of cents can make the actual maximum a few dollars lower.

items.value: Foreigners on Employment Pass / S Pass / Work Permit (and Miscellaneous Work Pass) make and receive no CPF contributions; contributions start from the day SPR status is granted.
items.evidence_quote: CPF contributions are not allowed for foreigners.
items.note: MOM agrees: 'employers of S Pass holders will not have to make Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions for them' (https://www.mom.gov.sg/faq/s-pass/do-i-have-to-make-cpf-contributions-for-s-pass-holders). A 2021 MOM parliamentary reply says this has applied to all foreigners since 2003.

summary:
12 of 12 searches used; 15 items checked: 12 confirmed, 1 corrected, 2 unverified. No candidate rate or ceiling was contradicted by an official source.

Direct page fetching was blocked, so every quote is the official page's text as relayed by the search tool's page reader, not a page I opened myself.

- **Corrected (cpf-relief-iras):** "voluntary contributions are not deductible" is too broad. IRAS excludes voluntary contributions above the compulsory amount, but allows relief on voluntary contributions to the MediSave Account. The rest of that item stands; the S$20,400 maximum is arithmetic, not an IRAS-quoted figure.
- **Unverified (low-wage-2025):** the 2025 table PDF was located but its text was not returned. The factors 0.51 and 0.345 fit the rule seen in the 2026 and 2027 tables (factor = 3 x employee rate), but I saw no official text for them.
- **Unverified (spr-gg-year2-2026):** partly confirmed. The 55-and-below row (9% / 15%, factor 0.45) and the factors 0.375 and 0.225 were read. The above-65 row and the employer rates of 6% and 3.5% for the older bands were not legible.
- **Confirmed with gaps:**
  - spr-gg-year1-2026: the employer 4% / 3.5% for bands above 55 was not read; the employee side is supported for every band.
  - low-wage-2026 and low-wage-2027: the above-70 factor 0.15 was not read. For 2026 the "> S$50 to S$500 employer only" row was also not read.
  - ow-ceiling: the 2027 figure of S$8,000 rests on CPF calling 2026 the last increase, not on an explicit 2027 line.
  - cpf-2025: the three unchanged bands are confirmed indirectly, from CPF saying only the 55-to-65 bands changed.

Official rate table PDFs, for a manual check of the gaps:
- 2025: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPF_contribution_rates_from_1_Jan_2025.pdf
- 2026: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/CPFcontributionratesfrom1Jan2026.pdf
- 2027: https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/employer/employer-obligations/documents/jan2027cpfcontributionrates.pdf
extra_findings: AW ceiling timing: CPF says the applicable AW ceiling depends on when the Additional Wage is due and payable - e.g. a 2025 bonus paid in 2026 falls under the 2026 AW ceiling. The AW ceiling applies per employee, per employer, per calendar year.

Derived from the confirmed ceilings: for someone at or above the OW ceiling all year, the AW ceiling is $102,000 - $96,000 = $6,000 in 2026 and 2027, versus $102,000 - $88,800 = $13,200 in 2025. Total CPF-liable wages stay at $102,000 in all three years.

Voluntary MediSave contributions qualify for IRAS relief (see cpf-relief-iras). The limits were not retrieved; the IRAS page 'Compulsory and voluntary MediSave contributions' has them. A tax optimiser should not treat all voluntary CPF as non-deductible.

IRAS also excludes from employee CPF relief: contributions made during an overseas secondment or posting, and contributions on Additional Wages above the cap where the employee works for two or more related employers.
IRAS: the $80,000 cap applies to the total of all reliefs per Year of Assessment, including compulsory and voluntary CPF; excess relief is disregarded and cannot be carried forward.

The CPF rate PDFs also carry F/G tables (full employer, graduated employee) for 1st- and 2nd-year SPRs, separate from G/G. The graduated employee factors match G/G (0.15 in year 1; 0.375 and 0.225 for the 55-60 and 60-65 bands in year 2). A calculator offering only G/G will misstate employer CPF for F/G cases, and employee CPF for anyone who has opted for full employee rates.
The SPR tables show maximum employee shares of $400 (1st year, 5%) and $1,200 (2nd year, 55 and below, 15%) for 2026, consistent with the $8,000 OW ceiling.

Age-band rule detail: on the birthday the employee is treated as having just turned that age and stays in the old band for the whole birthday month (CPF example: 55th birthday 13 Jan 2026 -> new rates from 1 Feb 2026).

2027: employers get a CPF Transition Offset equal to half of the 2027 increase in employer contributions, applied automatically. The extra 2027 contributions for ages above 55 to 65 go to the Retirement Account up to the Full Retirement Sum, then to the Ordinary Account. Neither affects the employee's tax.
